messages:
support_jane: FYI - Customer ACME reporting big p99 spikes from eu-west starting ~09:20 UTC. They gave request traces showing ~150-250ms extra on TLS handshake and a couple of HTTP retries.
aj: Got the customer id + sample traces?
support_jane: yes -> cust-acme-42, attached traces show client -> eu-west ingress -> unexpectedly routed via eu-central -> us-east -> back to eu-west (extra cross-region hop). timestamps in trace line up with 09:22 deploy window.
ops-bot: Deploy notice: egress-rebalance v3 rolled at 2025-11-03T09:22:14Z by eng-infra (GSLB weight adjustment, aggressive geo-rebalance enabled).
tom: Hmm that matches. I can see a shift in AS path for a subset of prefixes at 09:22 in our BGP collector. Looks like a tie-break changed causing some sessions to prefer a longer path via partner peer in eu-central.
maria: Reproduced from our synthetic probes: p95 fine, but p99 jumps ~180ms at ~09:25 for ~2% of requests to cust-acme endpoints in eu-west. Traceroute shows an extra inter-pop hop before TLS.
eli: Can someone paste the traceroute + dig outputs? quick checks: `dig +short svc.acme.example` and `dig +trace svc.acme.example` to confirm GSLB variant. Also run: ```traceroute -T -p 443 svc.acme.example || tcptraceroute svc.acme.example 443```
aj: Paste from probe: ```traceroute to svc.acme.example (54.93.12.8), 30 hops max
 1  10.0.0.1  0.7 ms
 2  eu-west-pop-1  1.2 ms
 3  eu-central-pop-2  160.4 ms
 4  us-east-pop-3  192.8 ms
 5  eu-west-pop-1  3.1 ms
```
support_jane: customer also said they started seeing auth errors timeouts on some calls (timeouts were within the latency window, no auth failures persisted after retry).
tom: Likely policy: aggressive GSLB weight + short DNS TTL caused caches to pick the wrong anycast/egress path during the rebalance. If the selected path has slightly different egress NAT or different upstream peer it can add handshake RTT.
maria: TTL was lowered to 10s during the change to accelerate propagation (I see the change in infra config history). That plus GSLB churn = cache thrash for some resolvers.
eli: Mitigations to try now: 1) rollback GSLB weight to previous stable profile, 2) restore TTL to 60s, 3) flush our egress POP local dns cache, 4) pin cust-acme to dedicated egress pool if available. I can push a rollback if infra approves.
aj: I rolled back the GSLB weights at 09:45 and flipped geo-rebalance off. Watching metrics: within two minutes p99 dropped from ~420ms -> ~50-70ms for most hosts. Still seeing a small tail ~120-150ms for a tiny fraction.
tom: Good. Next steps: create a short postmortem for config change process. We should avoid TTL=10 for production rollouts and add a canary window for aggressive rebalances. Also add route-preference fences to avoid cross-region detours during weight changes.
maria: I've opened INC-6321 and assigned to eng-infra for the egress-rebalance rollback validation + a follow-up to adjust TTL defaults.
support_jane: Can we confirm customer update? I'll message ACME support: short summary + remediation steps and ask them to confirm.
eli: To validate fully: run multi-region traceroutes and synthetic SSL handshakes from eu-west probes for the next 2 hours, and check for any residual AS path anomalies. I will kick off the probes.
aj: Thx all. Please add any residuals here. :thumbsup: :face_with_monocle:
